task_brief: Day 12 of "Foundations Portfolio and Private-Capable Presentation" (unit 6, grade 9) is a correction and reflection on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Assemble a foundations portfolio with an artist statement, documentation, a rights record, and a chosen private or public presentation mode. Today's work contributes to that by handling foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation at the correction and reflection stage, against the unit's wider topics of selecting and sequencing a cohesive body of work, artist statement drafting and revision, documentation standards for artwork, and presentation design for private or public modes. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Revise your earlier work on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation and document the revision rather than quietly replacing it. Build a revision log: what specifically was not working, what you now believe caused it, the change you made, and how you can tell the change helped. Keep the before and after side by side. Then write what pattern connects the problems you found — a habit of rushing one stage, a technique not yet secure, an intent never stated clearly — and one thing you will do differently that would catch it sooner. Honest documentation of a weak result scores fully here. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, and it belongs to "Foundations Portfolio and Private-Capable Presentation", which also covers separate topics such as selecting and sequencing a cohesive body of work. Close out with this check before you stop: For one corrected item, state the original error, its cause, and the check that would catch it next time. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on foundations portfolio and private-capable presentation rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
